proposed.explanation: While the architect may require the electrical panel relocation, the preferred resolution is for the mechanical consultant to adjust their system's routing first within their discipline. Structural accommodation is a more costly and time-consuming resolution that should only be used when routing adjustments are not feasible. Documenting unresolved clashes creates construction risk. All major clashes must be resolved before construction documents are finalized per the three-phase coordination framework. Route adjustment—moving ductwork to a new path—is a primary resolution strategy within the mechanical consultant's control. The mechanical engineer can typically find alternate routing paths that avoid conflicts. Clash resolution strategies follow a priority: route adjustment (least cost), system redesign, structural accommodation, equipment relocation. The architect maintains final authority over which strategy is applied.
